newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-76ERS SNAP 13-GAME LOSING STREAK, EDGING CELTICS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-76ERS SNAP 13-GAME LOSING STREAK, EDGING CELTICS.

text.p: The Philadelphia 76ers snapped a 13-game losing streak with a 127-125 victory over the Boston Celtics Thursday as rookie Allen Iverson scored 26 points, including three free throws in the final 30 seconds.
"It was just good to get this win and take some pressure off," Iverson said. "Honestly, I've liked the effort from my teammates. I wasn't frustrated. Hopefully we can build on this."

Jerry Stackhouse scored a season-high 38 points and Rex Walters had career highs of 27 points and nine rebounds and a season-high 11 assists for the 76ers, who avoided the longest losing streak in the NBA this season. The Suns lost their first 13 games.
Stackhouse and the Sixers got some advice from all-time great Julius Erving, who was at The FleetCenter.
"Dr. J was telling me personally to let the game come to me," said Stackhouse. "I think that rubbed off a lot on the other guys."

Two free throws by Stackhouse gave the 76ers a 117-115 lead with 2.2 seconds left in the fourth quarter. But Eric Williams fired a court-length inbounds pass to David Wesley, who put in a layup at the buzzer, forcing overtime.
Philadelphia (8-32) won for just second time in 25 games.

In Seattle, Hersey Hawkins made the go-ahead layup with less than three seconds left and Gary Payton stripped the ball from Isaiah Rider as time ran out to lift the SuperSonics to their ninth straight victory, 98-97 over the Portland Trail Blazers.

After Portland rookie Jermaine O'Neal dunked for a 97-96 edge with 8.6 seconds remaining, Hawkins broke free and received a well-timed pass from Payton under the basket to give the SuperSonics a 98-97 advantage with 2.8 seconds to go.
Rider received the inbounds pass and appeared headed for a 15-footer from the top of the key before Payton stripped him.

Detlef Schrempf scored 26 points, Shawn Kemp added 23 and 13 rebounds and Payton had 20 points and 12 assists for Seattle, which remained perfect in January and extended its home winning streak to 11 games.

Gary Trent and O'Neal posted career-highs with 24 and 20 points, respectively, for the Blazers, who lost for just the third time in 12 games. Trent was 9-for-11 from the field, while the 18-year-old O'Neal was 8-of-10.
Seattle has won 13 of its last 16 meetings with Portland, including all three this season.
In Sacramento, Mitch Richmond posted his third career triple-double and scored 22 of his 38 points in the fourth quarter as the Kings held off the Detroit Pistons 97-92.
Richmond scored all but six of Sacramento's fourth-quarter points. He added 10 rebounds and 10 assists as Sacramento won for just the fourth time in 11 games.
Grant Hill had 33 points and 10 rebounds and Otis Thorpe added a season-high 24 points and 13 rebounds for the Pistons.
In Phoenix, Karl Malone scored 27 of his season-high 41 points in the second half as the Utah Jazz pulled away for a 111-99 victory over the Suns.
Malone shot 16-for-28 from the field and grabbed eight rebounds as the Jazz won for the sixth time in seven games following a season-high five-game losing streak.
John Stockton had 23 points and 12 assists and Jeff Hornacek added 21 points for Utah.
Cedric Ceballos had 20 points and 10 rebounds as the Suns lost for just the second time in seven games with both setbacks coming to Utah.

In Denver, Mark Jackson had 15 points, 12 assists and a career-high 16 rebounds for his 11th career triple-double as the Nuggets posted consecutive wins for the first time in a month with a 94-84 victory over the Vancouver Grizzlies.
Jackson scored seven points in a 10-0 run that opened the game and gave Denver the lead for good.
LaPhonso Ellis scored 22 points and Antonio McDyess added 20 for the Nuggets.

In San Antonio, Kendall Gill scored 32 points and rookie Kerry Kittles added 10 of his 23 in the fourth quarter to lead the New Jersey Nets to a 103-95 victory over the Spurs for their first-ever sweep of the season series.
Khalid Reeves had 17 points and Jayson Williams recorded 14 points and 14 rebounds as the Nets won in San Antonio for the first time since November 1993, and just the third time in 26 games there.

Dominique Wilkins and Vernon Maxwell led the Spurs with 20 points apiece. Wilkins was returning after missing 10 games with a strained right knee. The Spurs lost for the eighth time in nine games and were held under 100 points for the 15th straight time.
